title: Evidence
description: A reference to the footage that supports one event, expressed as a seekable interval rather than a rendered file. Storing an interval plus the source means playback survives redeploys, and a clip whose footage is missing or expired is reported as unavailable instead of failing or being silently skipped.

evidence_id.description: Stable id, derived from the event it supports, so regenerating evidence does not orphan citations.

clip_start_offset_s.description: Start of the excerpt, media-relative. The excerpt is roughly one minute centred on the event, clamped to the source bounds.

clip_start_at.description: Absolute UTC start of the excerpt when a wall clock exists.

window_id.description: The surrounding 10-minute window, offered as a wider view when the footage is authorised for it.

seek_to_offset_s.description: Exactly where the player should start when it opens the source: the event moment itself, not the start of the excerpt. Tests assert the seek lands on the event.

player_ref.description: Opaque reference the app resolves to a player URL, e.g. 'player:src_demo_classroom?t=1830'. Kept opaque so the storage layout can change without rewriting stored records.

availability.description: Current state of the underlying footage. Anything other than available must surface to the user in words — the chat may cite the observation but must say the clip cannot be shown and why.

retention.description: How long this excerpt may be retained and served. Once expired, availability becomes footage_expired rather than the record disappearing.
